description: A component's verification of a platform access token (be-protocol P5; TOKENS.md 'Verification'). For each case: verify `token` with `defaults` overridden by `context`, and compare `valid` and, when false, `status`, `reason` and `domain`. `rule` names the failing check for debugging and is not compared. The JWKS holds four keys so that one file covers every algorithm; a real JWKS holds at most three. No case needs network: an unknown kid is unknown after the refetch.

cases.name: valid, signed by the previous key during a rotation
aud as a plain string equal to TENANT_ID
aud array with TENANT_ID among others
minimal claims: no roles, no dept_path, no locale, no tenant_id, no nbf
typ with another value is refused
expired but within the 60 s skew (now < exp + skew)
nbf in the future beyond the skew
nbf in the future within the skew
iat in the future beyond the skew
roles not an array of strings (P5.9)
HS256 keyed with the RSA public key (algorithm confusion)
header alg differs from the JWKS key's alg (RS256 header on the P-256 kid)
unknown kid (still unknown after the one refetch)
known kid, signature by another key
a Casdoor ID token, even if its key were in the JWKS (repro r1-09): aud is a client id, no typ claim
a platform refresh token presented as an access token (typ refresh, aud = issuer)
impersonation token (act user, ceil, dg) with delegation=true
ceil and dg when the authorization provider lacks delegation
agent deeper in a nested act chain when agents=false
iat more than 5 s before stale_since[sub]
stale_since of another sub does not matter
stale agent token: UNSUPPORTED_DELEGATION wins over TOKEN_STALE
exactly at exp + skew is expired (RFC 7519: now must be before exp)
